### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **47** documentable anchor(s).

**6** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`  _(via triggerType (symbol, a field of interface SubflowRetriedCallout), triggerType (literal, a string literal in retriedCalloutIn; a string literal on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via triggerType (symbol, a field of interface SubflowRetriedCallout), retried_callout_in_subflow (literal, a string literal in FLOW_UNBOUND_CAUSES; a string literal in describeUnboundReason), triggerType (literal, a string literal in retriedCalloutIn; a string literal on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/automation/workflows.mdx`  _(via triggerType (symbol, a field of interface SubflowRetriedCallout), triggerType (literal, a string literal in retriedCalloutIn; a string literal on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/getting-started/common-patterns.mdx`  _(via triggerType (symbol, a field of interface SubflowRetriedCallout), triggerType (literal, a string literal in retriedCalloutIn; a string literal on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/examples.mdx`  _(via triggerType (symbol, a field of interface SubflowRetriedCallout), triggerType (literal, a string literal in retriedCalloutIn; a string literal on a changed line))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class), triggerType (symbol, a field of interface SubflowRetriedCallout), triggerType (literal, a string literal in retriedCalloutIn; a string literal on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class), triggerType (symbol, a field of interface SubflowRetriedCallout), triggerType (literal, a string literal in retriedCalloutIn; a string literal on a changed line))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **172** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d4fbb4dbb655f1d1527eabeea0ef3af64f152663` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ca8f8e0a65ee0cf9e3f46f4621ca36216b99af84` — the merge of head `2b9a28a896310d06d49feba4213b498d867a8be4` into base `d4fbb4dbb655f1d1527eabeea0ef3af64f152663`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ca8f8e0a65ee0cf9e3f46f4621ca36216b99af84 && git checkout ca8f8e0a65ee0cf9e3f46f4621ca36216b99af84
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d4fbb4dbb655f1d1527eabeea0ef3af64f152663 2b9a28a896310d06d49feba4213b498d867a8be4 && git checkout -B drift-repro d4fbb4dbb655f1d1527eabeea0ef3af64f152663 && git merge --no-ff 2b9a28a896310d06d49feba4213b498d867a8be4

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d4fbb4dbb655f1d1527eabeea0ef3af64f152663
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d4fbb4dbb655f1d1527eabeea0ef3af64f152663` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2b9a28a896310d06d49feba4213b498d867a8be4`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts + packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/subflow-retry-guard.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-registration-checks.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-definitions.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/subflow-guards.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/http-nodes.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/http-nodes.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/subflow-region-suspension.test.ts, packages/lint/src/lint-flow-patterns.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/flow-problems.ts, ui/packages/i18n/src/namespaces/studio/en.ts, ui/packages/i18n/src/namespaces/studio/zh.ts + packages/triggers/trigger-record-change/src/record-change-trigger.ts (`triggerTypeToHookEvents`), packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/subflow-node.ts (read, not reviewed)

Face: published schema (`FLOW_UNBOUND_CAUSES`) and narrowing (`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` on PR body and changeset). Diff read against merge base `e540baf8`.

### ① Derived judgments

- `flow-registration-checks.ts`: the walk is factored out of `validateAfterSaveInlineRetry` into `walkRetriedNodes` / `flowRunRetry` / `inlineCalloutFix` / `afterRecordChangeTrigger` with no behaviour change: same visit-then-descend order, same `by ?? try_catch` innermost retry, same durable exemption, same sentence and site path. The after-save judge and the new gate now share one definition of "retried".
- `subflow-retry-guard.ts`: from an after-record-change caller, every `subflow` / `map` node (top level and any region) is followed into its child with the retry covering the call node (or the caller's whole-run retry) as the child's outer retry; otherwise the child's own whole-run retry applies, and inner `try_catch` retries are picked up by the shared walk. Deeper children are followed the same way. The `free:` / `retried:` seen-key ends call cycles without missing a flow reached first unretried and later retried. Children are resolved through `flowCallKey`, the same key the other halves use.
- The child's own `errorHandling` retry really does re-run the call when called as a subflow: `subflow-node.ts` runs the child through `engine.execute`, whose catch hands an `errorHandling: retry` flow to `retryExecution`. So the gate's retry positions match what the engine does.
- `engine.ts`: the new half runs last, after the disabled-subflow, save-notice and region halves; its record is cleared when a flow gets past it, read last by `describeUnboundReason` (gate order), carried across slot moves, dropped by `withdrawFlow`, and re-asked by `rejudgeSubflowCallers` for bound callers (live reading) and unbound ones (record). The warn is said once per distinct reason.
- `http-nodes.ts`: the inline send is moved into `sendInline` unchanged. The durable no-outbox fallback now branches on `onSavePath(context)` (`afterInsert` / `afterUpdate` / `afterDelete`, exactly the after-phase events `triggerTypeToHookEvents` produces). A `subflow` / `map` child spreads its caller's context, so it inherits the event, as the docblock says. The background promise has both handlers, so no unhandled rejection; the failure is logged at `error` with the consequence and the fix. Off the save path the inline fallback is untouched (pinned by the `beforeUpdate` control with its four attempts).
- Tests cover each retry position, a grandchild, decline → re-arm on republish, three arming controls, and the three after-phase events for the background send. The PR records ablations for both changes. 61 check runs on this head succeeded, 11 skipped, none failed; mergeable clean.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/service-automation` minor with the BREAKING banner (a flow armed before is now not armed; a durable no-outbox node on the save path no longer reports a response or fails the node) and ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: right, since no stored flow can be rewritten to keep its author's meaning. `@objectstack/spec` minor: one value added to an output enum, matching the precedent of `suspending_subflow_in_region`. `Metadata-protocol: semantic` fits the changed meaning of `durable: true` on a host with no outbox. UI changeset `patch`, `Clause-②: no`: right, it only adds a label for the new cause.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Published schema: `FLOW_UNBOUND_CAUSES` gains `retried_callout_in_subflow`, with its jsdoc row and the type-level `Eq` pin updated. The one exhaustive consumer in the repo (`flow-problems.ts` `UNBOUND_CAUSE_KEYS`) gets the key, with en and zh strings (the studio namespace holds only those two locales). No governed path in the diff.
- Nit (does not block): `@objectstack/lint` is bumped `minor` for a text-only change (one fix sentence and one explanation line); `patch` would do. Harmless.
- Nit (does not block): `onSavePath` reads the run's `event`, so a run that suspended and is resumed later (when no save is waiting any more) also takes the background send for a durable no-outbox node instead of the inline fallback. It only loses the inline fallback's response on a host already missing the outbox, and `durable: true` already means the run does not see the outcome, so no change is needed now.

### ④ Design judgment

Against the published contract on `main`: `FLOW_UNBOUND_CAUSES` is documented as the closed set `/_status` may report, and every existing value has its own remedy; a new cause for a new decline with its own remedy is the documented way to extend it, and keeping it a decline (registered, not armed, re-judged when a callee changes) rather than a registration refusal follows the region half for the same load-order reason. The narrowing serves ruling 6810500711 letter D (a save never waits on an outside system) and closes the two gaps #32515 left: a retry reached through a child, and a durable node falling back inline. Sending once in the background on the save path, with a loud `error` on failure, is the right reading of `durable: true` when no outbox exists, and it keeps the arm-time verdict free of a registry that fills at `kernel:ready`. First-party flows of either shape: 0 in `examples/**`, as the body says. No must-fix or should-fix.
